body.en: if (condition) statement; runs the statement only when the boolean condition is true. if … else chooses one of two blocks. An *if-else*-if ladder tests conditions from the top and runs the first block whose condition is true, skipping the rest. A nested if is an if inside another if; an else always pairs with the nearest unmatched if (the dangling else rule), so use braces to show the intended pairing.

points.en: else pairs with the nearest if
Use { } for blocks of more than one statement

body.en: *switch* is neater when one variable is compared with many constant values (menus, day numbers, grades). if is needed for ranges (marks >= 90), for conditions on several variables, and for real numbers or booleans, which switch does not accept. Forgetting break is a common error: execution then falls through into the following cases until a break or the end of the switch.
